children: Singapore's central bank may keep policy unchanged following its "surprise exchange rate policy hold," says MUFG Bank's Michael Wan in a report. The Monetary Authority of Singapore says it is "well-positioned to respond effectively to any risk to medium-term price stability," the senior currency analyst notes. The MAS also says "the current appreciating policy band will allow the S$NEER to continue to strengthen and lean against anticipated near-term rise in imported inflation," Wan adds. The MAS statement "sounds like the central bank might remain on hold for now unless the situation changes," the analyst says. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
